problem.title: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station

blocks.label: PUMPS AT THESE KM. ADD 3 MORE.

cover.promise: You'll solve it for **any k** with one binary search.

slides.title: Pumps on a highway
slides.scene: A highway has petrol pumps at km 1, 3, 12 and 16. You may build 3 more. Make the longest drive between two pumps as short as you can.

blocks.text: The 9 km stretch hurts most. How should the 3 new pumps be shared?

slides.title: The real problem
slides.lead: Add k stations so the largest gap between neighbours is as small as possible.

blocks.text: New pumps at 6, 9 and 14 leave gaps 2, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2.
Up to 5,000 stations at up to 10⁹, and k up to 100,000. Answer to 2 decimals.

slides.try_first: Share 3 pumps among the gaps 2, 9 and 4 by hand. What is the best longest gap?

slides.title: Try every share
slides.lead: Give each gap some pumps and space them evenly. Then try every way to share k.

blocks.text: Right for 3 pumps. With k up to 100,000, the shares are far too many to try.

slides.title: Guess the answer
slides.lead: Pick a longest gap d and count the pumps it needs. Smaller d, more pumps.

quickcheck.question: With 5 new pumps instead of 3, can the longest gap be 2?
quickcheck.answer: Answer: yes. d = 2 needs exactly {{pumps_needed(STATIONS, 2)}} pumps: 0 + 4 + 1.

slides.title: Binary search on d
slides.lead: Post 32's idea, on real numbers. Fits: try smaller. Too many pumps: go bigger.

blocks.text: Like tuning an old radio dial: each turn is half the last, and you close in on the station.

slides.title: Count, then stop
slides.lead: A gap g needs ceil(g / d) − 1 pumps. d fits when the total is at most k.

blocks.text: d is a real number, so stop when high − low < 0.000001, not when they meet.
Start with high = the whole road: that d needs no pumps.

final.caption: {{ROUNDS}} rounds later the range is under 0.000001.

slides.title: Count the pumps
slides.lead: For one guess d, add up the pumps every gap needs.

after.text: A 9 km gap at d = 4 needs 3 pieces, so 2 pumps.

lines: low = d    // too many: go higher

items.label: Time
items.note: L = road length, ε = 0.000001: about 50 rounds.

slides.pattern: Binary search on a real-number answer, with a count-and-compare check.

blog.summary: Minimise the largest gap after adding k stations: binary search the gap d, counting the stations each guess needs.

worked.name: GeeksforGeeks Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station

blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (the post's example, k = 0, the GFG and LeetCode 774 examples, one huge gap with up to 100,000 new stations), 5,000 random stations up to 10⁹ with k = 100,000, and random small and large cases
blog.tested_against: an exact brute force that hands out stations one at a time to the gap whose pieces are longest, using fractions
blog.tested_extra: Answers are compared to 2 decimals, as GFG asks; inputs where a rounding tie falls within 0.000001 of the answer are left out. The rounds in the walk-through and the hint numbers come from running the code.

caption.first: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station (GFG, LeetCode 774) solved with binary search on the answer, on real numbers.
lines: Guess the longest gap d. A gap g then needs ceil(g / d) − 1 new stations, and a smaller d always needs more.
So binary search d: it fits, go lower; too many stations, go higher. Stop when the range is under 0.000001.
